title: An open map with irreducible fibres is bijective on irreducible components
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces. Assume that (a) $f$ is open, i.e. $f(O)$ is open in $Y$ for every open $O\subseteq X$, and (b) for every $y\in Y$ the fibre $f^{-1}(y)$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] (in particular nonempty, so $f$ is surjective). Then for every irreducible component $T$ of $Y$ the preimage $f^{-1}(T)$ is an irreducible component of $X$, for every irreducible component $W$ of $X$ the image $f(W)$ is an irreducible component of $Y$, and the maps $T\mapsto f^{-1}(T)$ and $W\mapsto f(W)$ are mutually inverse bijections between the sets of irreducible components of $Y$ and of $X$.
